props.title: Ordinary People
props.initialSlug: Family deals with loss of oldest son

sections.content: Robert Redford's directorial debut Ordinary People revolutionized how Hollywood portrayed family trauma and mental health. The film's unflinching examination of upper-middle-class dysfunction shattered the perfect suburban facade, influencing later works like American Beauty (1999) and Little Children (2006). Through the story of the Jarrett family dealing with one son's death and another's suicide attempt, Redford crafted an intimate psychological drama that stood in stark contrast to the blockbuster era's escapism. Donald Sutherland and Mary Tyler Moore deliver career-defining performances as parents trapped in emotional paralysis.

sections.content: The film's influence on depicting therapy in cinema cannot be overstated. Judd Hirsch's portrayal of Dr. Berger created the template for authentic therapeutic relationships on screen, setting a new standard followed by Good Will Hunting (1997) and Silver Linings Playbook (2012). The sessions between Timothy Hutton's Conrad and Dr. Berger avoid melodramatic breakthrough moments, instead showing the gradual, painful process of healing from trauma.

Ordinary People also marked a crucial shift in how Hollywood depicted mothers. Mary Tyler Moore's Beth Jarrett subverted the loving maternal stereotype, presenting a complex woman unable to process grief or show affection. This paved the way for exploring maternal complexity in films like Terms of Endearment (1983) and August: Osage County (2013), where perfect motherhood myths crumble under psychological scrutiny. sections.content: The film's DNA is evident in contemporary family dramas like Marriage Story (2019) and The Father (2020), which similarly explore how trauma reverberates through family systems. Modern filmmakers continue drawing from Redford's techniques: naturalistic dialogue, emphasis on small moments, and the use of silence as emotional punctuation. The film's influence extends to television, with shows like "Six Feet Under" and "This Is Us" exploring similar themes of family grief and healing.
